key_insight: Synthetic crystal structures enable diffusion pretraining that improves materials property prediction without requiring new DFT relaxations for every generated structure.
engineering_relevance: Fast machine-learned relaxation offers a practical route to expanding structurally diverse pretraining datasets while reducing reliance on expensive quantum-mechanical calculations.
method: Generate crystals through perturb-and-relax, MatterGen sampling, and protostructure enumeration.
Use machine-learned interatomic potentials where structural relaxation is needed.
Compare coordinate denoising with VP and sub-VP diffusion pretraining using a randomly initialized Orb-v2 backbone.
evidence_signal: All synthetic-pretraining conditions numerically outperform random initialization on seven MatBench tasks; scaling protostructures from 20k to 165k matches or exceeds MP-20k pretraining on most tasks in an eight-task study.
watch_item: The fixed 400-epoch scaling protocol increases both dataset diversity and optimization updates, so its gains cannot be attributed to data scale alone.
paper_title: Synthetic Crystal Data Generation for Diffusion Pretraining in Material Property Prediction
